text: What is the core claim of perdurantism (four-dimensionalism) about how objects persist through time?
choices: Objects are wholly present at each moment they exist and have no temporal parts.
Only the present moment exists, so persistence is a succession of wholly present objects.
Objects persist by having distinct temporal parts (stages) at different times, just as they have spatial parts at different places.
Ordinary objects do not really persist; there are only simples arranged object-wise.
explanation: Perdurantism holds that an object is a four-dimensional whole composed of temporal parts, one at each time it exists. The tempting distractor (option 0) states endurantism (three-dimensionalism), the direct rival, on which the object is wholly present at each moment with no temporal parts at all.
